:::{#cor-self-outer-product-psd}
#### A self outer product is positive semidefinite

For a vector $\vx$,
the [self outer product](linear-algebra.qmd#def-self-outer-product) $\soprod{\vx}$
is [positive semidefinite](#def-positive-semidefinite).

:::

::: proof

Let $\matr{A} = \tp{\vx}$, the $1 \times n$ [matrix](linear-algebra.qmd#def-matrix) whose one [row](linear-algebra.qmd#def-matrix-row) is $\vx$.
Then

$$
\ba
\stprod{\matr{A}}
&= \tp{\matr{A}} \matr{A}
&& \text{(definition of the Gram matrix)}
\\
&= \tp{\paren{\tp{\vx}}} \tp{\vx}
&& \text{(substitute } \matr{A} \text{)}
\\
&= \vx \tp{\vx}
&& \text{(the transpose of a transpose is the original matrix)}
\\
&= \soprod{\vx}
&& \text{(definition of the self outer product)}
\ea
$$

So $\soprod{\vx}$ is the [Gram matrix](linear-algebra.qmd#def-gram-matrix) of $\matr{A}$,
and @thm-gram-properties says that a Gram matrix is [positive semidefinite](#def-positive-semidefinite).

:::
